title: The shepherds (Luke 2:8–20)
hookLine: the news goes first to men on the night shift, and the angels sing glory to God in the highest
carry: good news goes to the outsiders first
tomorrow: is waiting your whole life for something ever worth it?

lines: LUKE SENDS IT TO A FIELD.
cards: When news breaks at 3 a.m., who sees it first? Not the people asleep. The nurse on her break.
The trucker at a gas station. The guy stocking shelves under the bright lights. In Luke, that's who gets the news of this birth: men outside Bethlehem, keeping the night watches over their flock.
Big news usually goes to palaces first. Luke sends it to a field, and to the night shift.

teach.h: THE NIGHT SHIFT, IN THE FIELDS.
teach.b: Luke doesn't romanticize them. Some historians think shepherds then sat near the bottom of the social ladder; others think that's overstated.
Either way, David, the great king, had been a shepherd boy from Bethlehem, so the scene holds both: the low job and the royal line.

An angel appears, they're terrified, and the angel says what Mary and Joseph heard too, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Fear not; for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, that shall be to all the people."
The sign isn't a crown. It's a baby lying in a manger, a detail shepherds would know on sight.

teach.h: GLORY TO GOD IN THE HIGHEST.
teach.b: Then the sky fills with angels: "Glory to God in the highest; and on earth peace to men of good will." Here's one to tell a friend: if you've been to Mass on a Sunday outside Advent and Lent, you've heard that line.
It opens the Gloria, so every week the people in the pews pick up the shepherds' song. The shepherds go with haste, like Mary on day twenty-two, find it all as they were told, and tell everyone.
And Luke adds one quiet line about Mary: "But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart."

how: Catholics sing the Gloria, which begins with the angels' song, at Mass on most Sundays and feasts, and the shepherds' Mass, at dawn on Christmas Day, is one of the traditional Christmas Masses.

o: Night workers who heard of the birth first
Wise kings who followed a star to Bethlehem
Temple priests who announced the birth

games.q: who's in the fields — tap the pairs.
p: fear not: good tidings of great joy
a baby lying in a manger

s: the shepherds and the wise men came to the manger together
the shepherds are only in Luke; the magi are only in Matthew, who has them come to a house.
the angels' song opens the Gloria sung at Mass
the shepherds kept the news to themselves
they told what they'd been told, and everyone who heard wondered.

games.q: your school wins state. the principal wants the first thank-you to go to the big donors. by Luke's pattern, who hears first?
o: the night custodians and the bus drivers.
games.why: Luke sends the news to the night shift, not the palace, and the outsiders spread it. good news goes to the outsiders first.

practice: Count on your fingers the people who worked last night so your morning could happen: whoever baked the bread, drove the truck, kept the hospital lights on, cleaned the station, maybe you.
Try to reach ten, and give each one a second of thanks as the finger goes down.

wordCard.voice: The shepherds. The night shift outside Bethlehem, first to hear and first to tell.

orig.note: Latin: glory to God in the highest. the angels' song, and the first words of the Gloria at Mass.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: good news goes to the outsiders first, and they're the ones who spread it. Until tomorrow.
